summary: Rewrote getDeveloperAction in mcp-server/src/tools/workflow-next-action.ts using a per-WP priority evaluation loop from §14.2.
Priority 1 (BLOCK_FOR_REWORK_LIMIT): uses rework_counts.implementation directly — legacy compat shim (rework_count fallback) removed.
Priority 2 (RESUME_OR_CANCEL): stale implementation pipeline detection via extractStalePipelineAction.
Priority 3 (CONTINUE_PIPELINE): new priority — fires when isActivePipeline returns true for implementation.
Priority 4 (REWORK direct): most recent implementation FAIL — now correctly precedes IMPLEMENT (P6).
Priority 5 (REWORK downstream): hasDownstreamFail + hasDownstreamReengagedSince guard — fires only after temporal re-engagement is confirmed.
Priority 5b (WAIT_FOR_DOWNSTREAM): new — fires when downstream FAIL exists but developer already re-passed and downstream hasn't re-engaged yet.
Priority 6 (IMPLEMENT): IN_PROGRESS WP with no implementation pipeline.
Priority 7 (CLAIM_WP): READY WP with dependencies satisfied — replaces legacy IMPLEMENT-for-READY pattern.
Added imports: isActivePipeline, hasDownstreamFail, hasDownstreamReengagedSince from workflow-helpers.
Updated rework-circuit-breaker.test.ts: last test expectation changed from IMPLEMENT to CLAIM_WP (READY WPs now return CLAIM_WP).
Updated workflow-handoff.test.ts: added sequential timestamps to setupAndGetDevAction helper; updated 5 test expectations to reflect temporal guard and BLOCKED WP scope change.
Added 9 test cases in describe('Developer action logic') in workflow-next-action.test.ts.
npx tsc --noEmit: clean. npx vitest run: 738/738 passed.

comments.note: The per-WP evaluation loop in getDeveloperAction iterates all WPs for each priority per WP. A slight optimization would be to break early once P1 fires for any WP, but since it already returns on first match this is moot—already optimal.

BLOCKED WPs with downstream FAILs are now silently WAIT from Developer's perspective. A future improvement could be to surface a specific WAIT_BLOCKED_DOWNSTREAM action so the Developer knows WHY they are waiting, rather than a generic WAIT.

summary: Reviewed getDeveloperAction in mcp-server/src/tools/workflow-next-action.ts. Full 7-priority per-WP evaluation loop is correctly implemented per §14.2.
P1 (BLOCK_FOR_REWORK_LIMIT): uses rework_counts?.implementation only — legacy scalar fallback confirmed removed.
P2 (RESUME_OR_CANCEL): delegates to extractStalePipelineAction for stale impl detection.
P3 (CONTINUE_PIPELINE): correctly guards active non-stale impl pipelines via isActivePipeline.

P5/P5b (REWORK downstream / WAIT_FOR_DOWNSTREAM): hasDownstreamReengagedSince temporal guard gates the split correctly. Test cases 4 and 5 with correctly-ordered timestamps validate both branches.
P6 (IMPLEMENT): fires for IN_PROGRESS WPs with no impl pipeline.

comments.note: hasPassImpl local variable at P5 is a defensive redundancy: if execution reaches P5, P3 has already eliminated active IN_PROGRESS impl pipelines and P4 has eliminated direct FAIL impl pipelines. The only case remaining where hasPassImpl would be false is when there is no implementation pipeline at all — which P6 (IMPLEMENT) handles. The variable is harmless and aids readability, but a future reader may wonder why it's needed. A short comment explaining the invariant would make the intent explicit.

Test Cases 3 and 9 exercise near-identical scenarios: both verify that P4 (REWORK for direct FAIL) fires before P6 (IMPLEMENT). Case 9 labels itself a 'priority ordering' test but notes 'Same as case 3.' They share the same setup. Merging into a single parameterized test or giving Case 9 a distinct scenario (e.g., three WPs to prove the ordering holds across more than two) would eliminate redundancy without losing coverage confidence.

BLOCKED WPs with downstream FAILs fall through all priorities and ultimately return WAIT. The Developer debt note (from implementation pipeline) flags this accurately. No action needed now, but consider a WAIT_BLOCKED_DOWNSTREAM action when the PM action system matures to give the Developer a specific reason for waiting rather than a generic WAIT response.

The test helper makeWpDetail hardcodes assigned_to: 'Developer'. QA Case 7 (CLAIM_WP for QA) correctly sets assigned_to: 'QA' explicitly. The Developer Case 7 relies on the default. This is fine but could trip up a future developer adding a test who doesn't notice the implicit assignment. A comment on the helper would prevent confusion.
